title: Biennial controlled-substance inventory
rule_summary: After the initial inventory, a registrant must take a new controlled-substance inventory at least every two years. Current DEA regulation permits any date within two years of the previous biennial inventory; the related statutory general-physical-inventory language does not authorize delaying the DEA inventory beyond that regulatory two-year window.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate can apply biennial inventory requirements to a pharmacy-practice scenario without substituting a nearby rule.
exceptions: The statutory coordination with a regular general physical inventory does not extend the DEA regulatory deadline past two years from the previous biennial inventory.
common_confusions: Reading the statutory general-inventory coordination language as permission to delay the DEA inventory beyond the two-year regulatory limit.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1304.11(c) and current 21 U.S.C. 827(a)(1) checked together on 2026-08-14.
